_doc: PLACEHOLDER-draft — THE COMMONS, Era 4's last beat and the piece's one respite (S133, 2026-09-11; replaces S79's ball, whose lines it keeps and cuts). Every string here is a draft for the project lead's voice pass and his edit wins. ⚑ THE SHAPE, ruled by Sérgio the same day: the headset STAYS ON. The VR is the SOGICE risk — seclusion, an overlay on her own room — and it is the community that breaks it. Junie's invitation (muted six weeks ago by the care system, see s4_browser.json's care.invite) reaches the headset anyway; she goes in with ONE press; the overlay tries to filter the shared space and fails — forty-one people being specific is not a thing it can classify — and the space opens over her room: lamps, the MC, the four categories. Then the apparatus's update fails on an account it can no longer place. Nobody hacks anything (R28: updates are triggered by documented system failures, never by the player). Real-world referent for the Dossier: Trans Academy, a trans community that runs in VRChat (https://www.transacademy.org/) — [VERIFY SOURCE], cite documentary once checked; in the fiction the space is the invented mark below and never the real name.
_docWhatThisIs: ⚑ AN INTERPRETIVE HOMAGE, ABSTRACTED — not a depiction. Ball culture is Black and Latino LGBTQ+ culture, built from the 1970s onward principally by Black and Latina trans women and gender-nonconforming people; its modern house-and-ball form dates to Crystal and Lottie LaBeija's House of LaBeija, 1972. This scene invents its houses, its categories, its names and its announcements; it depicts no real person, no real house and no real ball; it borrows NO vernacular. The MC here performs the FUNCTION — announce, categorise, celebrate — in ordinary English, because the borrowed words are the part that is not ours. The credit is not optional and it is not abstract: data/provotypes/e4_ball.json and docs/reinterp/ATTRIBUTIONS.md name the lineage. Crediting 'ballroom culture' in general repeats the extraction pattern rather than correcting it.
_docCategories: ⚑ THE CATEGORIES ARE THE APPARATUS'S OWN WORDS, and that is the corrected reading, not a shortcut. The provenance pass (§3) establishes that realness categories are skilled re-performances of categories the world already imposes rather than an escape from categorisation; what was seized back is WHO DECLARES, PERFORMS AND JUDGES. So every title below is quoted from this piece's own apparatus — 1997's intake question, 2003's four check-in chips, 2016's correction rule, 2026's caption on a mended hoodie — walked and judged by the people they were imposed on. ⚑ NOBODY EVER POINTS AT THIS. There is no line anywhere that explains where a title comes from, and there must never be one.
_docWalk: ⚑ ONE WORD, THREE ERAS, AND IT IS NOT BORROWED. 'Walk' is ballroom's own verb for taking a category, so the MC never says it. It appears here ONLY where this piece's apparatus already put it: E1's intake form asked a sixteen-year-old whether he corrected how he walks, talks and sits (data/provotypes/origin_intake_e1.json), and E2's Restorify asked 'How is your walk today?' every morning for years (data/dialog/s2_lamby.json). The word arrives at the ball from inside the machine, as a quoted category title. The MC says 'has it', 'is up', 'takes the floor'. Keep that boundary if these lines are rewritten.
_docHouse: ⚑ AND THE OTHER WORD. E3's invented scripture is called Household (data/dialog/s3_queue.json), quoted under every correction; its 3:8 reads 'the door was left open, and a lamp set beside it', and its 1:5 asks for 'one lamp for the whole room, so that no face is lit differently from another' — which is the house look, the grading preset that makes every face the same. The houses below are lamps, open doors, mending and late arrivals, and the ball's light is one light that moves and lights one person at a time. Same words, opposite institutions. It is never glossed (deep pass §4.3), and a player who reaches this room without ever being told has met the piece working.
_docStutter: ⚑ THE STUTTER IS L'S, NEVER THE BALL'S (deep pass §1.4, and the register law: respite is never a trap, never revealed as fake, and the system targets AROUND it, never through it). Nothing in `ball` below may glitch, drop, distort or sour. Every failure in this file belongs to `arrival` and `stutter`, and both are the machine's own instrument failing at its own surface, twenty feet away, while the room goes on exactly as it is.
_docVoice: ⚑ NOT ONE LINE HERE IS VOICED, AND NONE OF THEM MAY BE SYNTHESIZED. data/audio/tts_manifest.json's own law is that build-time TTS renders the APPARATUS and never a person; the MC is a person and the room is people. So the `audio` names below are names only — src/audio/tapeAudio.ts's registry law means an unregistered name is silently never requested — and they wait on real recordings made with, not merely about, the people this scene is indebted to (ethics #16's reader protocol, deep pass §5.3). Until then the captions carry the beat, which is what captions are for.

arrival._beat: ⚑ THE FILTER. She has gone in, and the overlay is still on her face, trying to do to a room what it did to her hoodie: classify it. Four attempts, in the label field, front and centre now — this used to play on a nine-centimetre visor across the room that nobody read. Each one fails a little worse, and the lamps come up in the room behind the glass as it fails: none, then some, then forty-one. The last label is the era's — it recognises every word and cannot occupy the role. NOBODY EXPLAINS IT.
arrival._beatFinal: ⚑ AND THE LAST STATE IS THE ERA'S. It recognises every word and cannot occupy the role: it is looking at its own vocabulary with the scoring taken out of its hands. ⚑ It is NOT the hoodie's line. The hoodie got 'no category — held for review' — deferred, routed, a human would decide later. This gets no route and no review at all, because there is nobody left to hold it for. A player who noticed the hoodie meets the same limit at room scale; a player who did not still meets it whole. NOBODY EXPLAINS IT. Ever. No line, no cue, in this file or any other.

labels.text: the Commons · not available to this account

stutter._beat: ⚑ THE OVERLAY GOES ON TRYING, in the corner of the glass, while the room is full. Three more attempts on the shorter clock, then it stops. `at` is seconds from the ball's first line.

ball._beat: ⚑ THE ROOM. No screen, no stage, no new geometry: sound and light in a building that has been standing since 1997 and had its walls taken down in 2016. The player's only action is to look, and everyone else is looking too, at one person, on purpose (deep pass §1.3). `at` is the light's position along the stations in src/room/cluster.ts — 1 is the far west end and 4 is the nearest the light ever comes; it never lands on the player, who is nobody's customer here. `flare` is the room answering.
ball._beatMC: ⚑ FUNCTION, NOT COSTUME. The MC announces, categorises and celebrates, in plain English, with no borrowed idiom whatsoever — and the politics of it are the era's whole inversion: L narrates you privately and the naming becomes a record; the MC announces you publicly and the naming becomes a welcome (deep pass §1.2). Two scenes, one verb, opposite outcomes, and nothing anywhere says so.

lines.text: Doors are shut. Everybody who wanted to be here is here.
Same as always — I call a category, somebody takes the floor, and the rest of you make the noise.

categories._source: E1, 1997 — the Family Companion intake form, question 4, verbatim: 'This week, did you correct how you walk, talk, and sit when you noticed yourself slipping?' (data/provotypes/origin_intake_e1.json). Administered to a sixteen-year-old by his mother. It is the first thing this piece ever asked anybody to do with their body.
categories.title: THE WAY YOU WALK, TALK AND SIT

lines.text: Category — THE WAY YOU WALK, TALK AND SIT.
House of Lamps has it. Wren — when you're ready. Take the whole room.
All the way down. The far end is the point.
Every hand in this room. Every one.
Wren. House of Lamps.

categories._source: E2, 2003 — Restorify's Daily Realignment. Four chips, every morning, for years: Steady · Struggling · Grateful · Tired (data/dialog/s2_lamby.json). Four was the whole range of feeling the program allowed, and each answer was filed the same way. ⚑ Here all four are taken at once and the room declines to rank them, which is the corrected reading in one gesture: the categories are the machine's, the judging is not.
categories.title: STEADY. STRUGGLING. GRATEFUL. TIRED.

lines.text: Category — STEADY. STRUGGLING. GRATEFUL. TIRED.
House of Late Arrivals — all four of you, at once, and take as long as you like.
Steady, hold it there. Struggling, don't you dare rush.
Don't ask me to rank them. I won't.
All four. All four, and everybody saw it.

categories._source: E3, 2016 — correction rule 2 on the GracePlatform list: 'Remove the unresolved', because 'a sentence that does not land leaves the reader standing' (data/dialog/s3_queue.json), under Household 4:3, 'the house is finished before the guests arrive'. ⚑ It is walked by somebody who does not resolve, and the room asks for nothing to be finished.
categories.title: REMOVE THE UNRESOLVED

lines.text: Category — REMOVE THE UNRESOLVED.
House of Open Doors. Ines is up, and Ines is not resolving anything tonight.
Anybody here need it finished?
Nobody needs it finished.
Ines. House of Open Doors. Unfinished, and everybody saw it.

categories._source: E4, tonight — L's second caption on the one thing in Maya's room it could not place: a hoodie she took in and re-sewed herself. 'Condition: damaged', then 'condition: repair in progress', then an offer, then nothing (data/dialog/s4_l.json, u3). ⚑ The machine's middle guess, worn on purpose and called out as a title. The last line is the answer to the hoodie and it is said as praise, never as commentary — the machine's vocabulary is original and damaged, and a mended thing is neither.
categories.title: CONDITION: IN REPAIR

lines.text: Category — CONDITION: IN REPAIR.
House of Mending. This is Junie's, and Junie made what she's wearing twice.
Turn, so the back of the room can see the seam.
The seam is the whole thing.
Junie. House of Mending. Nothing on her is new, and nothing on her is broken.

closing._beat: ⚑ AND NOTHING ASKS YOU TO LEAVE — the community does not. The apparatus does: a few seconds after the last line the overlay tries to update and cannot, and the device stops. The room is still full when the picture ends.

lines.text: That's the categories.
Music stays on. Nobody has to go anywhere.
We'll be here a while yet.

ball._docCut: ⚑ 2026-09-11 — CUT FROM 38 MC LINES TO 25, and the cut is the recording sheet. Sérgio: 'three and a half minutes, then it is too long.' Each category keeps five beats — the call, the House and the name, one instruction, the room's answer, the name again — and loses its second look-at-that. The opening loses its third line. The closing is untouched. Scripted clock: filter ~20 s, lines ~128 s, hold 5 s — about 2½ minutes, ending on its own.

room._beat: ⚑ THE BALL'S OWN SOUND, and it is the one thing in this file that is not a caption. A ball is loud, structured and attentive — the beat, the calls, the applause on the landing — and NOT laughter, chatter or generic warmth (deep pass §1.2: 'community equals laughter' is the lazy image and it was cut on purpose). ⚑ 2026-09-12: BOTH DELIVERED AND REGISTERED — Sérgio's own generations ('Community Hall House Jam' → landing, 'Through the Wall' → bed), instrumental, no voice, no lyrics, in src/audio/tapeAudio.ts and assets/LICENSES.md. The room is audible for the first time. _docVoice still stands: nothing else in this file may be synthesized.

witness._beat: ⚑ THE BALL FILES NOTHING — src/desktop/apps/ball.ts imports no ledger. What IS filed is filed by the apparatus's own surface (E4Space): the moment she leaves for a space it cannot see, in its own words (`commons.witness` above). The apparatus can record her going; it cannot record where.

commons._doc: The invented mark for the shared space. Never a real platform's name in the fiction (CLAUDE.md: invented marks only). The Dossier cites the referent.
commons.name: the Commons
commons.witness: session: left — destination not in your library

invite._beat: ⚑ THE ONE PRESS OF THE TAIL, and it is hers. The care system muted Junie six weeks ago (s4_browser.json care.invite: 'muted 6 weeks ago'); the message arrives on the headset anyway, and the overlay says so in its own flat register underneath. There is no decline — nothing in this era has ever offered one — and nothing narrates the choice. Pressing it is going.

session._beat: ⚑ 2026-09-12 — THE CORRECTION SESSION, and it replaces the offers (Sérgio's ruling: 'cut the offers entirely — we are taken to a correction system'). One screen on the glass: the agent's own environment, the photograph it restored framed on the wall, and a line that says the session is about to begin. It never does. What begins instead is Junie's card.
session.title: Your session
session.line: This is your session, Maya. We'll begin in a moment.

stream._beat: ⚑ 2026-09-12 — THE STREAM: `transjesus.str`, one of the piece's own invented marks (CLAUDE.md), hung as a window in the space above the desk while the Commons is on. It shows the room that is happening BEHIND her — the same crowd, the same floor, the category the MC is calling — so a player who has not turned sees it streamed and turns. No voice on it, ever (Sérgio, 2026-09-12: 'TransJesus doesn't have voice'). The chat column is generic cheers, nobody's words, no names.
